text: Percolator is Anatoly Yakovenko's perpetual futures engine for Solana. It can list any market without permission. But a new market starts empty, and whoever lists it holds its keys.

Percolator Vaults fixes that. Anyone can open the market for a Pyth price feed. A vault program lists it, owns every key, and becomes its liquidity, from one shared pool per asset. Nobody can pause, change, or drain it.

Let's open a market. I connect a devnet burner wallet and grab test USDC. Opening takes two transactions: create the vault, then list the market with its Pyth feed. I choose nothing else. Every market runs on the same rules, and as the opener I earn ten percent of its fees, forever, with no other powers.

On the Bitcoin market, the vault is the counterparty. It sizes every fill from its own value, up to three times its net asset value, so every deposit deepens the market. I open a trading account, add margin, and go long. The trade is queued, and fills at the first Pyth price published four seconds later: a price nobody, not even me, could know when I traded, so nobody can front-run the vault.

Liquidity providers all deposit into that same pool. Deposits and withdrawals settle together at one price at the end of each epoch, about six minutes on devnet, so nobody trades against a stale share price. Depositors share ninety percent of the market's fees.
Every trader is ranked from on-chain data. Wallets we used to seed demo activity are labelled as seed.

Under the hood, the vault's address is derived from the price feed, so an asset can never have two pools. The vault program is the matcher that Percolator calls on every trade. If a trader holds a position to block withdrawals, anyone can make the vault close its own position. Thirty-nine tests run it against Percolator's production binary, including attack scenarios.
Percolator Vaults. Keyless perp markets, with liquidity built in, that nobody can front-run. Live on Solana devnet today, and built to go to mainnet with Percolator.
